case_name: Mahesh Chander and another v State Of Delhi
respondent:
State Of Delhi
Supreme Court of India

3 April 1991
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION : Criminal Appeal Nos.432 & 628 of 1979. From the Judgment and Order dated 4.5.1979 of the Delhi High Court in Crl. A.No.323 of 1976.
The Judgment was delivered by: S. Ratnavel Pandian, J.
1.  The above appeals by special leave u/art. 136 of Constitution of India are directed against the correctness and legality of the judgment dated 4th May, 1979 of the High Court of Delhi in Criminal Appeal No.323/76.
2.  These two appellants were accused Nos. 2 and 1 respectively before the 8th Additional Sessions Judge and they took their trial in Sessions Case No. 38/75 on the charge that on 28.5.1975 at about 3.30 a.m. in Pitam Pura within the jurisdiction of Punjabi Bagh Police Station both appellants in furtherance of their common intention committed murder of Hanumant Singh, the deceased herein and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 302 read with 34 IPC. facts: The deceased Hanumant Singh was the son of Harkishan Singh (PW-6).

The facts of the case briefly stated are as follows:
The deceased persistently asked his wife PW-4 to bring back the ornaments telling her that her father and brother had intended to grab the same.
On 25.5.75 the deceased rebuked PW-4 and asked her to bring the ornaments from her parents, but PW-4 expressed her helplessness.
As PW-4 had gone to her parents house, the deceased brought Km.
PW-11 was woke-up and found the appellant Mahesh Chander sitting over the deceased and securing him firmly.
The deceased shouted 'MAR DIYA, MAR DIYA, BACHAO BACHAO' (Being killed, being killed, save me, save me).
At this point of time PW-11 escaped from the scene house and went to the house of her father (PW-5) to inform him.
On the way PW-11 met PW-3 at some distance but despite enquiry by PW-3, PW-11 could not give any reply and she was dumb-sticken.
By that time, PW-3 came by the side of the house of the deceased.
When they were at a distance of 8 to 10 paces, they saw the appellants running towards Shakurbasti.
Thereafter all the four namely, PWs 1,3,5 and 6 entered the house and found the deceased dead.
issues: The correctness and legality of the judgment dated 4th May, 1979 of the High Court of Delhi in Criminal Appeal No.323/76.
Whether the evidence of PW-11 is reliable and trustworthy?
petitioner_arguments: Despite the prolonged deliberation, neither the name of appellant Mahesh Chander nor the presence of Km.
The First Information Report was registered at about 8.15 a.m.
PW-5 who is none other than the brother of the deceased and an Advocate by profession did not mention the fact of his daughter (PW-11) informing him about the murder of the deceased to any one.

The evidence of PW-11 is nothing but a tissue of falsehood and her evidence is demonstrably proved to be unworthy of credence for more than one reason that being that PW-11 who was by then aged about 13 would not have slept alone in the house of the deceased.
Secondly if she had been an eye-witness to the occurrence, she would have immediately come forward with a statement that she saw both the appellants by mentioning their names.
Thirdly PW-5, the father of PW-11 who had filed a criminal case against the deceased for offences u/ss.

No adverse inference can be drawn against the appellant Mahesh Chander on his refusal to take part in the identification parade since PW-5 has admitted that he had seen Mahesh Chander at the police station.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution examined PWs 1,3, and 11 as eyewitnesses to the occurrence.
PWs5 and 6 were examined to speak about the appellants running away from the scene after the commission of the crime.
The evidence of PW-11 is reliable and trustworthy.
